cards.key: The formula of methylamine is CH₃NH₂. When an amine and a carboxylic acid combine, an amide and water form. A peptide bond also forms with the loss of water.

once.soru: The bad smell of fish comes from amines. Squeezing lemon on it reduces the smell. Why?

secenekler.yazi: The acid forms a salt with the amine
secenekler.neden: An amine is a base, and the acid in lemon turns it into a salt that does not evaporate.
The lemon smell helps, but the main effect is that the amine turns into a salt.
Lemon does not cook the fish. The acid in lemon neutralizes the basic amine.

cards.p:
• The functional group decides a compound's properties.
• A 1° alcohol becomes an aldehyde first, then an acid. A 2° alcohol becomes a ketone, and a 3° alcohol is not oxidized.
• Aldehydes give a positive Tollens test, and ketones do not.
• An acid and an alcohol give an ester and water. A fat and NaOH give soap.
• An amine is a base, and a peptide bond is an amide bond.

quiz.q: Propanoic acid and methanol are heated with concentrated H₂SO₄. Which ester forms?
quiz.e: An ester's name gives the alcohol's alkyl group (methyl) first, then the acid with -oate (propanoate). So CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ is methyl propanoate.
y: You reversed the order. The alkyl part comes from the alcohol (methyl), and the -oate part from the acid (propanoate).
The acid has 3 carbons (propanoic). Ethanoate comes from a 2-carbon acid.
The alcohol is methanol. So the alkyl part is methyl, not propyl.

quiz.q: How many grams of NaOH are used when 0.2 mol of triglyceride (fat) is completely saponified? (NaOH = 40 g/mol)
quiz.e: Each triglyceride has three ester bonds, so 1 mol of fat uses 3 mol of NaOH. 0.2 × 3 = 0.6 mol of NaOH is needed. That is 0.6 × 40 = 24 g.

quiz.q: Sort each alcohol by the first product it forms when oxidized with K₂Cr₂O₇.
quiz.e: Ethanol and 1-propanol are primary alcohols and become aldehydes first. 2-propanol and 2-butanol are secondary alcohols and give ketones. (CH₃)₃C−OH is a tertiary alcohol. The carbon carrying −OH has no H, so it is not oxidized.

quiz.q: X and Y both have the formula C₃H₆O. X gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent, and Y does not. What could X and Y be?
o: X and Y are the same compound
quiz.e: A silver mirror points to an aldehyde (propanal). A ketone (propanone) does not give a positive Tollens test. The two are functional group isomers with the same formula. The formula of 2-propanol is C₃H₈O.
y: Tollens' reagent oxidizes aldehydes. Propanone is a ketone, so it gives no silver mirror.
The same compound gives the same reaction. Different behavior shows two separate isomers, an aldehyde and a ketone.
The formula of 2-propanol is C₃H₈O, and it gives no silver mirror. Propanal does give a silver mirror.

kimya-her-yerde.summary: Learn about cleaning products, polymers, medicines, food and farm chemistry.

once.soru: What is the chemical name of the soda used to make a cake rise?

secenekler.neden: Baking soda is NaHCO₃. When heated it releases CO₂ and makes the dough rise.
NaCl is table salt.
CaCO₃ is limestone.

cards.p: Soap is the sodium or potassium salt of a fatty acid. The tail of a soap molecule sinks into the grease, and the head faces the water. The sphere that forms this way is called a micelle. The micelle keeps dirt suspended in water.

etk.soru: Tap the parts of the soap molecule and the micelle.

noktalar.acik: The tail is a long hydrocarbon chain. It is nonpolar, so it loves grease, not water.
The head is the ionic −COO⁻ end. It interacts well with polar water molecules.
Nonpolar grease does not dissolve in water. The soap's tails sink into the grease.
Water molecules surround the heads on the micelle's surface. This keeps the dirt suspended in water.
A polar solvent. The micelles carrying dirt spread through the water and rinse away.

cards.key: The ionic head loves water (hydrophilic) and the hydrocarbon tail loves grease (hydrophobic). Soap is made from fat and NaOH (with glycerol as a byproduct).

cards.p: Detergents are synthetic cleaners made from petroleum, and their structure is similar to soap. They don't form scum with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺, so they lather even in hard water.

once.soru: What happens to a plastic bottle thrown into the sea?

secenekler.neden: Plastic breaks down very slowly in nature. It crumbles into microplastics.

secenekler.yazi: It rots in a few months
secenekler.neden: Microorganisms can't break down most plastics.
Plastics are nonpolar, so they don't dissolve in water.

cards.p: The substance that makes a medicine work is called the active ingredient. Too small a dose does nothing, and too much is poisonous. Antibiotics act on bacteria, not on viruses.

once.soru: What happens if someone with the flu takes an antibiotic?

secenekler.neden: The flu is a viral disease, and antibiotics act only on bacteria. Unnecessary use leads to resistance.
Antibiotics don't kill viruses.
An antibiotic gives no immunity, because it is not a vaccine.

cards.p: Food spoils because of microorganisms, enzymes and oxygen. Cooling, drying, salting and pasteurization slow spoilage down. Additives are listed on the label with E numbers.

once.soru: How does salt in brine keep food from spoiling?

secenekler.neden: Concentrated salt draws water out of microorganisms by osmosis. So the microorganisms can't multiply.
Salt does not produce heat.
Oxygen speeds up spoilage, and salt does not add oxygen.

cards.p: The values on a nutrition label are usually per 100 g. The use-by date is a safety limit, and the best-before date is about quality.

cards.p: Fertilizer gives plants nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Pesticides kill pests. Insecticides are used against insects, herbicides against weeds and fungicides against fungi. Too much fertilizer causes eutrophication in lakes.

once.soru: Rain carries excess fertilizer from a field into a lake. What happens in the lake?

secenekler.neden: Fertilizer feeds the algae too. As the algae rot, the oxygen in the water drops and the fish die.
Fertilizer pollutes the water, and the excess nutrients upset the balance.
The oxygen drops, so the fish die.

cards.p: Limescale is a basic deposit, and an acidic product (vinegar) dissolves it. Greasy dirt comes off with a basic product (soap, baking soda). Never put acid on marble or strong base on aluminum.

once.soru: Which removes limescale stains in the shower most easily?

secenekler.neden: Limescale is CaCO₃, and the acid in vinegar dissolves it.
Soap is basic. It removes greasy dirt, but it does not dissolve limescale.
Baking soda is basic too, and it does not dissolve limescale.

cards.p:
• Soap is a fatty acid salt, and it carries dirt into water by forming micelles.
• In hard water soap forms scum, but detergent lathers.
• Never mix bleach with acidic or ammonia cleaners.
• Plastic is a polymer and lasts a long time in nature.
• Watch the dose of medicines and read food labels.

quiz.q: Match each farm chemical to its job.
quiz.e: Insecticides, herbicides and fungicides are pesticides used against insects, weeds and fungi. Fertilizer doesn't kill pests. It gives plants nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

quiz.q: Sort each property under soap or detergent.
quiz.e: Soap is the Na or K salt of a fatty acid. It forms scum with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ and breaks down more easily in nature. Detergent is a synthetic substance made from petroleum, and it lathers in hard water too. Detergents with added phosphate can cause algae growth in lakes.

quiz.q: A bag of chips says 0.8 g of salt per 100 g. If you eat the whole 30 g bag, how many grams of salt do you get?
quiz.e: The values on the label are per 100 g. So 0.8 × 30 / 100 = 0.24 g of salt.

quiz.q: Someone mixes bleach with an ammonia glass cleaner to clean the windows. What happens?
o: They neutralize to salt and water
quiz.e: Hypochlorite reacts with ammonia and forms chloramine gases that burn the airways. Never mix bleach with acid or with ammonia.
y: Mixing two cleaners doesn't clean better. Together these two produce a toxic gas.
Ammonia is a weak base and bleach is basic too. What happens here is not neutralization but chloramine formation.
NaOCl reacts with ammonia and releases toxic chloramine.

enerji-kaynaklari.title: Energy sources and scientific advances
enerji-kaynaklari.summary: Learn about fossil, renewable and nuclear energy, green chemistry and nanotechnology.

cards.p: Sources that renew themselves quickly are called renewable. Sun, wind, rivers and geothermal (underground heat) are among them. Coal, oil, natural gas and uranium are nonrenewable. Electricity is not a source but an energy carrier.

etk.soru: Put each one in the right group.
ogeler: Its reserves are limited. Nuclear fuel counts as nonrenewable.
Electricity is produced from another source. It is not a source itself.
It is not found free in nature. It is produced by using energy.

cards.key: Hydrogen is an energy carrier too. Nuclear energy releases no CO₂, but it is not renewable, because uranium reserves are limited.

once.soru: Is the electricity you get from an outlet an energy source?

secenekler.neden: Electricity is produced from another source and carries the energy.
Electricity itself is not a source. What matters is what it was made from.
Electricity can be made from coal or from sunlight. So it is a carrier, not a source.

cards.h: Fossil fuels and the oil refinery
cards.p: Coal formed from buried plants, and oil and natural gas from plankton, over millions of years. Crude oil is separated by boiling point through fractional distillation.

cards.h: Combustion, CO₂ and the greenhouse effect
cards.p: Every fossil fuel gives CO₂ when it burns. CO₂ absorbs the infrared rays given off by Earth's surface and warms the atmosphere. This is called the greenhouse effect. Extra CO₂ strengthens this effect and leads to global warming.

cards.p: When the sulfur in fuel burns, SO₂ forms, and in the air this gas turns into H₂SO₄. Nitrogen oxides also give HNO₃. So the pH of rain drops below 5.6. This rain wears away marble and acidifies lakes.

cards.p: A solar cell turns light directly into electricity. A solar collector heats water instead. A wind turbine turns the kinetic energy of moving air into electricity with a generator. Neither releases CO₂.

once.soru: What does a rooftop solar collector with black pipes produce?

secenekler.neden: The collector uses the sun's heat to warm the water in its pipes.
Solar cells produce electricity. A collector only heats.
Hydrogen is produced by electrolysis. A collector only heats water.

cards.p: In hydroelectric power, the potential energy of water behind a dam turns a turbine. Geothermal power uses hot water and steam from underground. Wave and tidal power plants use the motion of the sea.

once.soru: At a dam, which energy of the water is turned into electricity?

secenekler.neden: Water stored up high turns the turbine as it falls.
Dam water is not heated. The energy of falling water is used.
The water does not react. The energy that comes from its height is used.

cards.p: Biomass is matter of living origin, such as wood, crop waste and manure. Bioethanol comes from sugar, biodiesel from vegetable oil, and biogas from waste that rots without oxygen.

once.soru: Farm animal manure is left to rot in a closed tank. Which fuel comes out?

secenekler.neden: Waste that rots without oxygen gives biogas, which is mostly methane.
Gasoline is made from crude oil.
The gas from rotting manure is mostly methane.

cards.p: In a nuclear power plant, the fission of 235U nuclei produces heat. This heat turns water into steam, and the steam turns a turbine. Spent fuel stays radioactive for thousands of years.

once.soru: How does a nuclear power plant produce electricity?

secenekler.yazi: Heat makes steam, steam turns a turbine
secenekler.neden: The heat of fission boils water, and the steam turns a turbine.
Electricity directly from light happens in a solar cell.
Uranium does not burn. Its nuclei split (fission).

cards.p: In a fuel cell, H₂ and O₂ react without burning. Chemical energy turns directly into electricity, and the only product is water. But hydrogen is not found free in nature and has to be produced.

once.soru: How should you travel 1 km to school to have the smallest carbon footprint?

secenekler.neden: Walking burns no fuel.
A car burns gasoline and releases CO₂.
A taxi is also a car and burns fuel.

cards.p: Green chemistry aims to prevent pollution from the start. To do this, it avoids creating waste, seeks high atom economy and uses safe solvents. Atom economy shows how much of the reactants' atoms end up in the product.

cards.p:
• Fossil fuels and uranium are nonrenewable, and sun and wind are renewable.
• Combustion gives CO₂ (greenhouse effect), and sulfur gives SO₂ (acid rain).
• Nuclear power plants use 235U fission and leave waste.
• A fuel cell makes electricity from H₂ and O₂.
• Green chemistry prevents waste. At the nanoscale, the surface-to-volume ratio grows.

quiz.q: Order the steps by which the sulfur in coal turns into acid rain.
quiz.e: When sulfur burns, SO₂ forms. In the air, O₂ oxidizes SO₂ to SO₃. In clouds, SO₃ gives H₂SO₄ with water, and the pH of rain drops below 5.6.

quiz.q: Quicklime is made from limestone: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. If the desired product is CaO, what is the atom economy in percent? (Atom economy = molar mass of desired product / molar mass of reactants × 100; Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
quiz.e: The molar mass of CaCO₃ is 100 g/mol, and that of CaO is 56 g/mol. The atom economy is 56 / 100 × 100 = 56%. The remaining 44% leaves as waste CO₂.

quiz.q: Match each technology with where it gets its energy.
quiz.e: A photovoltaic cell turns light into electricity, a wind turbine the kinetic energy of air, and a hydroelectric plant the potential energy of falling water. A fuel cell makes H₂ and O₂ react without burning. A nuclear power plant uses the heat of <sup>235</sup>U fission.

quiz.q: Which statement about hydrogen and fuel cells is true?
o: Hydrogen is a primary energy source found free and in large amounts in nature.
A fuel cell burns hydrogen and makes heat first, then electricity.
Hydrogen gas is easy to store.
The only product of a fuel cell is water.
quiz.e: Hydrogen is an energy carrier produced from water or natural gas by using energy. A fuel cell turns chemical energy directly into electricity without burning. Storing hydrogen gas requires high pressure or deep cooling.
y: In nature, hydrogen is mostly found in compounds and is produced by using energy. So it is a secondary source.
A fuel cell does not burn hydrogen. It turns chemical energy directly into electricity.
Hydrogen gas has little energy per volume. So it must be compressed or cooled, which makes storage hard.

yesil-kimya.title: Green chemistry and nanotechnology
yesil-kimya.summary: Learn to prevent waste from the start, get to know the nanoscale, and look at plastics and energy through a green lens.

cards.p: Green chemistry means designing products and processes to be harmless from the start. The first of its 12 principles is: preventing waste is better than cleaning it up after it forms.

cards.key: Using less and safer material, less energy, renewable feedstocks and products that break down in nature are also among the principles. The cleanest waste is the waste that never forms.

once.soru: Which is the greener solution for a factory?

secenekler.neden: Waste that never forms needs no treatment, energy or risk.
Treatment is good, but it uses energy. Preventing waste from the start is better.
Moving waste does not get rid of it. It only changes its location.

cards.p: 1 nm is one billionth of a meter. A strand of hair is about 80,000 nm thick. Particles 1-100 nm in size are called nanoparticles. At this size, the surface grows and the properties of matter change.

cards.p: Used tea leaf extract contains polyphenols. These reduce the Ag⁺ ions in silver nitrate to Ag atoms. The atoms gather as nanoparticles, and the solution turns yellow-brown.

cards.key: The extract coats the particles and keeps them from clumping. Pomegranate peel works too. Copper nanoparticles are made in a similar way.

cards.p: In the comparison, only the type of waste changes. Amount, temperature and time are kept constant. If the peak is near 420 nm and has a similar shape, the sample with the larger blank-corrected absorbance has made more nanoparticles.

cards.key: The independent variable is the waste type, and the dependent variable is absorbance. The blank contains only the extract, so the extract's own color is subtracted. If the peak shifts, the particle size is different, and amounts cannot be compared directly.

once.soru: You are comparing used tea leaf extract with pomegranate peel extract. What may you change?

secenekler.neden: A fair test has a single variable, and everything else is kept constant.
If two things change at once, you can't tell what caused the difference.
If everything changes, the results cannot be compared.

cards.p: Heavy metals such as lead, mercury and cadmium do not break down. Living things get rid of them slowly, so these metals build up in the body. Mercury becomes more concentrated as it moves up the food chain. This is called biomagnification.

cards.p: Silver nanoparticles kill germs, so they are added to socks. Washing releases them into water, and treatment plants cannot catch them all. In nature, they can also harm useful bacteria.

cards.key: Nanoscale size makes particles hard to separate from water. The solution is to cut needless use and design products to be safe from the start.

once.soru: When socks with silver nanoparticles are washed, where does some of the silver go?

secenekler.neden: With every wash, some of the particles get into the water.
The particles don't hold tightly to the fibers and decrease with each wash.
Silver does not evaporate. Water carries it away.

cards.p: Nano zinc oxide in sunscreen blocks UV rays without leaving a white film. Lipid nanoparticles carry mRNA vaccines. But breathable dusts and long-term effects are still a concern.

cards.key: Nano-coated glass cleans itself. The word "nano" on a product does not make it good or bad. What matters is the evidence and the purpose.

once.soru: A product says "nano" on it. Does that show the product is safe?

secenekler.neden: "Nano" only describes the size. Research shows whether it is safe.
Nanoscale size sometimes brings new risks too.
Being nano does not mean being natural or safe.

cards.p: Plastic smaller than 5 mm is called microplastic, and plastic smaller than 1 µm is called nanoplastic. The main sources are washing synthetic clothes and tire wear. Microplastics have even been found in human blood.

once.soru: What happens to a plastic bottle in the sea over time?

secenekler.neden: Sunlight and waves break plastic apart. The pieces get smaller but do not disappear.
Plastic stays in nature for hundreds of years.
Plastic does not dissolve in water.

cards.p: PLA is made from corn starch. Starch becomes sugar, fermentation turns the sugar into lactic acid, and the lactic acid polymerizes. At home, you can also make a film from starch, water, vinegar and glycerol.

cards.p: Some bacteria break down sugary waste without oxygen and release hydrogen. This is called dark fermentation. One glucose gives at most 4 H₂. When hydrogen burns, only water forms.

cards.key: The reaction is C₆H₁₂O₆ + 2H₂O → 2CH₃COOH + 2CO₂ + 4H₂. The yield depends on the waste type, pH, temperature and time.

cards.key: Efficiency is found by dividing the electrical power by the incoming light power and multiplying by 100. The best cells reach 13-15%. This cell works well in dim light, but it has a short lifetime.

etk.soru: 100 mW of light falls on a 1 cm² cell. Change the current and voltage the cell gives. What is the efficiency?

once.soru: 100 mW of light falls on a cell, and the cell gives 10 mW of electricity. What is the efficiency in percent?

secenekler.neden: The efficiency is 10 ÷ 100 × 100 = 10%.
90% is the part that does not become electricity.
Efficiency is the electrical power divided by the light power, multiplied by 100.

cards.p: AI data centers use a lot of electricity and cooling water. But AI can quickly screen new battery and catalyst materials and manage the power grid efficiently.

cards.key: The impact depends on which energy it runs on and what it is used for. The question to ask is: are the savings bigger than the energy used?

once.soru: How can you tell whether an AI project is good for the environment?

secenekler.neden: If it saves more energy than it uses, it helps.
Running fast does not show any benefit to the environment.
Being new does not mean being eco-friendly.

cards.p:
• Green chemistry prevents waste from the start. Microscale work is an easy way to do this.
• Nanoparticles are 1-100 nm in size and can be made with waste extracts.
• Heavy metals and nanoparticles can build up in nature.
• Microplastics get smaller but do not disappear.
• PLA, hydrogen from waste and dye solar cells are green options.

quiz.q: Sort each practice by whether it fits green chemistry.
ogeler: Throwing used batteries in the trash
quiz.e: Green chemistry prevents waste from the start and chooses renewable, safe materials. A needlessly large experiment creates waste. Used batteries release heavy metals. Microbeads get into water as microplastics.

quiz.q: Match the terms with their definitions.
quiz.e: The nanoscale is 1-100 nm. Microplastics are under 5 mm. A metal that living things cannot get rid of builds up step by step along the food chain. Polyphenols in the extract reduce silver ions to metal.

quiz.q: Put the steps of making PLA in order (first at the top).
quiz.e: Starch breaks down into sugar, bacteria turn the sugar into lactic acid, and lactic acid molecules link together to form the PLA chain.

quiz.q: You are studying how the type of household waste affects hydrogen production by fermentation. Which of these is a control variable that must be kept constant?
quiz.e: Waste type is the independent variable, and hydrogen volume is the dependent variable. Temperature, pH, amount of waste and time must be kept constant. Otherwise you can't know what caused the difference.
y: Waste type is the independent variable that you change.
Hydrogen volume is the result you measure, so it is the dependent variable.
If you change several things at once, you can't know what caused the difference.
